title: The angle you turned something to is a number you can read and type
goal: You can turn a shape by dragging the knob above it, but nothing anywhere tells you what angle it landed on, and there is no way to type 45 or to put it back to straight except undo. Anyone laying out a screen or writing down a spec needs the number, not just the gesture.
notes:
Verified by reading the code on 2026-09-09. Rotation is fully real: Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerTransform.swift holds rotation, skew and both flips, Sources/PhotonzCore/TransformDrag.swift does the maths, Sources/Photonz/CanvasPointerDrags.swift:349 drives the knob, and Sources/PhotonzRender/DocumentRenderer.swift:858 composites it. The only thing missing is a readout: Sources/Photonz/GeometryInspector.swift has X, Y, W and H and no angle, and grep finds no Rotation or Angle row anywhere in Sources/Photonz.

This is finishing a gesture that already ships, not a new feature, so no decision card. Follow the pattern the geometry fields already set (docs/design/ui-building.md, "Landed: typed position and size"), including the arrow-key stepping and the refusal sentence when a number is clamped.

One thing NOT in scope, filed separately if it matters: Sources/Photonz/CanvasGroups.swift:82 says a group never offers the rotate knob because groups translate and nothing else. Do not try to make groups turn in this task; just make the field say so honestly.
acceptance: The Position and Size section reads back the angle of whatever is picked, and a typed angle turns it, in the same shape as the X, Y, W and H fields beside it
Typing 0 puts a turned layer back to straight, and one undo takes back a typed angle in one step
A mixed selection and a layer that cannot turn (a group, a locked layer) each read the way the section already handles those cases, rather than showing a live field with nothing behind it
To see it: Scripts/probe-app.sh, draw a rectangle, drag the knob above it, and read the angle in the panel; then type 45 and watch it turn
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

log.note: Read the model. Rotation lives on Layer.transform (radians), the knob commits through EditorState.commitLayerTransform, and Position & Size is LayerGeometryField (four CGRect fields) + LayerGeometrySelection. Plan: add a fifth field case 'rotation' (label A, degrees) so Mixed, read-only, caption and click-to-explain all come for free, with the write routed to a transform commit rather than a frame commit.

Adversarial pass before building. The mock had nothing to say here, so the argument was with the section itself. Making the angle a fifth LayerGeometryField rather than a control of its own was the shortest version that delivers the value: Mixed, the read-only look, the click that explains itself, the arrow keys and the caption all come for free instead of being invented again. Rejected: a Transform section (a new home for one number), and a bare number with no unit (the section says px once in its caption, and a bare 45 under a W of 296 reads as another length, so A carries a degree sign). Cut: nothing decorative was proposed. The one thing that had to be added rather than reused is a second write path, because an angle is not in the box.

Built. Core: LayerAngle (the one place radians and degrees meet, plus wrapping a turn to the shortest way round), LayerGeometryField.rotation with label A, LayerGeometryEditing.canRotate mirroring the canvas rule for the knob, Member.angle, turning(to:)/steppingRotation, caption and unit-marked text. App: EditorState.previewRotations (the angle half of previewMoves, so the field follows the knob live), commitRotations for one undo step across a selection, and a third row in GeometryInspector.

Widened the locked sentence from "its position or size" to "its position, size or angle" and dropped a second locked wording, so the section still has ONE lock sentence now that it has three kinds of number.

Verified on the real app, not assumed. Scripts/playtest/angle-field-walk.json is new and passes: A reads 0 on a fresh rectangle, a shift-held knob drag lands 45 AND the held mid-drag capture already shows 45 (so the field follows rather than jumping), typing 0 straightens, one undo returns 45, arrow steps 1 and shift 10, 370 lands on 10, an arrow shows a dash, a locked layer shows 10 degrees as plain text, a group shows a dash. Also re-ran every walk that touches this section: geometry (2), panel (18), text (13) and 13 more named ones, all green. Scripts/test.sh green at 5331 tests.

Second adversarial pass, on the built thing. Rough and filed: a group/frame/copy cannot turn at all (task a-group-turns-like-anything-else), and it is unconfirmed whether the panel offers typeable numbers on a piece inside a copy (task find-out-whether-position-and-size-takes-numbers, p2 because I could not reproduce it). Left as judgement calls, recorded in the audit: the keyboard steps 1 and 10 while the knob's shift snap is 15, and the layer thumbnail still draws a turned shape straight.
Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-09-angle-field.json, with two real screen captures (Screen Recording was granted).

Position & Size gained an A row: the angle in degrees, following the rotate knob live, typeable across a selection in one undo step, 0 puts a layer back to straight. Fifth LayerGeometryField in PhotonzCore (LayerAngle + turning(to:)), written to the layer transform via EditorState.commitRotations; groups, lines, arrows and calipers read a dash with a sentence, a locked layer reads its angle. Verified by Scripts/test.sh (5331 green, two new core suites) and a new Scripts/playtest/angle-field-walk.json plus every walk touching this section. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-09-angle-field.json with two real screen captures. Committed 9087833e and pushed.
